name: Amplitude
summary: Product analytics: funnels, retention and behavioural cohorts, plus session replay and experimentation.
best_for: product teams who want everyone looking at the same behavioural data — the free 2 million events a month is a real working tier, not a demo
skip_if: you need page-and-session web analytics rather than product events, because that is a different tool and much cheaper; also skip it if your event volume is unpredictable and you cannot get a rate card
honest_knock: Unlimited seats is genuinely unusual and worth the credit — you are not taxed for letting the whole team look. The cost lands on events instead, and events are the thing you control least: an instrumentation change or a growth spurt moves your bill without anyone choosing to upgrade. What the plan cards do not print, the page's own bill estimator does, and we read the whole Plus ladder there on 17 September and again, unchanged, on 4 October 2026. What it shows is how little volume buys you: the marginal million events costs $94 a month at the bottom of the ladder and still $86.25 at the 70-million ceiling where Plus stops, and above that ceiling nothing is published. And 'expanded packages are priced as a percentage of your platform plan' means the add-ons scale with your bill rather than with your usage of them — the more events you send, the more the extras cost, whether or not you use them more. Get the per-event rate in writing before you instrument.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Plus (3 million events) · per month, from the bill estimator on the pricing page
pricing.notes: (2026-09-17, re-read on their own pricing page on 2026-10-04 and again on 2026-10-21, unchanged) Free $0 with 2 million events a month, permanently, no card required and no time limit. Plus starts at $0 with the first 2 million events free and scales up to 70 million events; a card is required. The plan card prints no rate, but the bill estimator on the same page does: on 17 September and 4 October 2026 it priced 3 million events at $94 a month, 10 million at $720, 30 million at $2,450 and 70 million, the Plus ceiling, at $5,865, with annual billing 20% lower at every step. Growth and Enterprise are quote-only, both described as event-based pricing. The page states every plan includes the full platform and unlimited seats, and that expanded packages are priced as a percentage of your platform plan. Startups with under $10 million in funding and fewer than 20 employees are offered one free year on Growth, applied for rather than self-served. The published caps that do differ by tier are session replays (10,000 a month on Free and Plus, 20,000 on Growth, 50,000 on Enterprise), active experiments (one on Free and Plus, two on Growth and Enterprise, more as an add-on) and agent sessions (5,000, 10,000 and 20,000). Plus can also be metered on monthly tracked users instead of events: the comparison table caps Plus at 700K MTU or 70M events, and the page's estimator prices that ladder from $52 a month for 1,000 MTU to $5,338 for 700,000 (read 4 October 2026).

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 30 October 2026 on the free plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported two made-up events from a CSV without writing code and tried the project's raw data export.
findings: Setup leads with an AI prompt to paste into a coding tool, but there is also a no-code route: 'CSV of Events' under Integrations. No card was asked.
The CSV import needs an event type, a time and a user or device ID; any other column can become an event property. Both of our test events showed up as received within about a minute.
Event times arrived correctly: our UTC times were shown in Dutch time, including the change from summer to winter time.
The project's 'Export Data' asks for a range of UTC dates. For our fresh events it returned nothing: a 404 for the event dates, and no file for the upload date, about 20 minutes after the import.
The setup screen shows your project's API key in plain sight, so take care with screenshots.
not_tested: The raw data export once processing has caught up
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?

vendor_mcp.what: Hosted server at mcp.amplitude.com/mcp (mcp.eu.amplitude.com for the EU), OAuth, streaming HTTP. Queries charts, dashboards and notebooks, manages experiments, feature flags and cohorts, reads session replays, and reads and writes the tracking-plan taxonomy including branch workflows.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their docs: "Any existing Amplitude customer can use Amplitude MCP from an MCP-capable client." No tier is named and no extra cost is mentioned. Write calls are gated by permission rather than by plan — creating or updating requires the Use MCP (write) RBAC action.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
